messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: storing sums of log probabilities
parts:
Hi everyone,

We've had a question on twitter about recording the sums of log probabilities (https://twitter.com/fbuderman/status/1272951989228445698).  This has come up before and might be something in need of a more general solution.  Any input on use cases?

Meanwhile, here is a workaround that uses a proxy sampler (i.e. not really an MCMC sampler, but invoked via the list of samplers) to record the sum of arbitrary log probabilities.  The default is to include all stochastic nodes, but any nodes can be specified.  Multiple of these can be included.

-Perry

-----

library(nimble)

# A proxy "sampler" that isn't really an MCMC sampler but will be called
# in the list of samplers.  It will store the sum of nodes give in control$logProbNodes
# in the target node.
storeLogProb <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    logProbNodes <- model$expandNodeNames(control[['logProbNodes']])    
  },
  run = function() {
    sumLogProb <- model$getLogProb(logProbNodes)
    model[[target]] <<- sumLogProb
  },
  methods = list(reset = function() {})
)

# A utility function to modify an mcmc configuration to use storeLogProb.
# Arguments are:
# mcmcConf: an mcmc configuration such as returned by configureMCMC
# model:    an uncompiled model object
# target:   the node name to be used for storing the sum of log probabilities
# nodes:    the nodes whose sum of log probabilities will be stored in the target node.
#           default value for nodes is all stochastic nodes in the model (except target).
configureStoreLogProb <- function(mcmcConf, model, target, nodes) {
  if(missing(nodes))
    nodes <- model$getNodeNames(stochOnly = TRUE)
  nodes <- nodes[ nodes != target ]
  mcmcConf$removeSamplers(target)
  mcmcConf$addSampler(type = 'storeLogProb', target = target, control = list(logProbNodes = nodes))
  mcmcConf
}

# Example:
# This model will have real nodes a[1]...a[10] (a toy with no data, but that doesn't matter for demonstration  of storeLogProb).
# And it will have a proxy node "sumLogProb" that will be used for recording the sum of log probabilities
modelCode <- nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:10) a[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  sumLogProb ~ dnorm(0,1) ## dnorm(0,1) will not be used.  It just establishes sumLogProb as a stochastic node.
})

model <- nimbleModel(modelCode, inits = list(a = rnorm(10), sumLogProb = 0))
mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(model)
configureStoreLogProb(mcmcConf, model, 'sumLogProb')
mcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf)

cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = model)
samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc, niter = 10)
samples[,'sumLogProb']

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: storing sums of log probabilities
parts:
Hi Perry

Many thanks for this - it's a great solution!! 

For models where convergence to the target distribution is slow, tracking sumLogProbs provides a simple indication of whether you should extend the burn-in period. In these cases, I'll often write a loop that will perform a chunk of burn-in and then check if there is a non-negligible trend in sumLogProbs to decide if further burn-in chunks are required. 

I'm currently collaborating with a team that have mixing issues with a model that has a very large number of latent variables. My current approach of tracking logProbs for all the latent variables (and using rowSums after doing MCMC) uses a huge amount of RAM. Your solution will greatly reduce the memory requirements in this work.

Best
David

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: storing sums of log probabilities
parts:
If there's sufficient interest, then I could see this becoming a feature in NIMBLE's core MCMC, e.g.:


conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
conf$addMonitors(...)
conf$addSampler(...)
conf$addSumLogProb(c("x", "y", "theta"))
## build, compile, and run MCMC
samples <- runMCMC(1000)
samples[, "sumLogProb"]      ## this column would contain the sum-log-probs of "x", "y", and "theta"

Or something like that.  I'd welcome thoughts or feedback on this idea from anyone.

Daniel
